deviations.qemu_behavior: QEMU v9.2 virtio_error marks the device broken and, with VIRTIO_F_VERSION_1 negotiated, sets NEEDS_RESET and notifies a configuration change for malformed queue state.
deviations.bridgevm_behavior: Checked split-queue access refuses unreadable or overflowing ranges. Invalid descriptor chains may remain pending or be completed with zero used length depending on the device; no matching broken-device/NEEDS_RESET/configuration-change transition is implemented.
deviations.impact: Recovery from malformed queue configuration differs. This static comparison does not claim a conforming-driver failure or a live guest observation.

deviations.qemu_behavior: QEMU v9.2.0 flushes namespaces without checking the returned error before publishing shutdown complete. Clearing SHN clears SHST; a combined SHN plus EN-clear write ends with reset CSTS=0 (hw/nvme/ctrl.c and hw/nvme/ns.c).
deviations.bridgevm_behavior: Native NVMe normal and abrupt shutdown flush both attached backends before SHST=10. A failed flush leaves SHST=01 and sets CFS=1; queue processing stops until reset. SHN=00 does not cancel shutdown. A combined SHN01/10 plus EN-clear resets first, then performs shutdown with RDY=0; a successful flush sets SHST=10, while failure leaves SHST=01/CFS=1. Plain reset/re-enable clears shutdown and fatal status.
deviations.impact: These are conservative model failure and ordering policies permitted by NVMe 1.4 sections 3.1.5, 3.1.6, 7.6.2 and 10.5, not a claim that the specification mandates this exact ordering. Failed synchronization is never reported as successful shutdown. Deterministic tests cover the existing backend contract; memory and read-only overlays remain volatile, and no physical durability, live guest shutdown or Windows criterion is established.
